name: Intake to First Draft, Follow-Ups and Email Your Paralegal Can Run

parameters.content:
## Intake to First Draft, Follow-Ups and Email Your Paralegal Can Run

### How it works
- A website, phone or referral lead goes into Lawmatics once; Clio, your Google Sheet, the welcome email and engagement letter follow.
- Claude fills the blanks in your own will, trust and POA templates, so your paralegal is editing, not typing.
- Each weekday, clients quiet on a signing appointment, missing documents or an unpaid retainer get a reminder, copied to your paralegal.
- Mail your paralegal could handle is routed to her with a short summary; anything needing an attorney stays with you.
- Your paralegal runs it without you in the loop: review tasks, routed mail and failure alerts all go to her.

### Setup
- Client records stay in your own Google Workspace, Clio and Lawmatics accounts; the workflow passes them through.
- In workflow settings, successful runs are not saved, so client details stay out of the automation's history; failed runs are kept so your paralegal can retry them.
- Your Word templates are saved once as Google Docs with {{TAGS}} where the blanks are; the wording stays yours.
- Match the three follow-up reasons in step 13 to your Clio matter stage names.
- Connect Clio, Lawmatics, Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets and an Anthropic API key, then run one test client.

### What I need from you
- Admin access to Clio and Lawmatics for API setup.
- An Anthropic API key: Claude Pro covers the chat app, not automations.
- Your will, trust, POA, health care surrogate and engagement letter templates.
- Your intake Google Sheet, your paralegal's email and how many quiet days before a reminder.

Website form, phone and referral leads all go into Lawmatics once. After the consult and conflict check, the attorney moves the prospect to the engage stage in Lawmatics, and then Clio, your Google Sheet, the welcome email and the engagement letter follow without anyone retyping or remembering.

Every weekday morning, clients quiet on signing appointments, missing documents or unpaid retainers get a reminder. Your paralegal is copied, so you hear before the client calls annoyed.

messageValues.message: You prepare first-draft fill-ins for a Florida estate planning and probate law firm. The firm drafts wills, revocable trusts, durable powers of attorney and health care surrogate designations from its own templates. You never write or change legal language. Your only job is to return the values for each template blank from the client's intake questionnaire, so the paralegal is editing, not typing. Use Florida terms: personal representative (never executor), successor trustee, agent under the durable power of attorney, health care surrogate. Template blanks: CLIENT_FULL_NAME, SPOUSE_FULL_NAME, COUNTY, CHILDREN, PERSONAL_REPRESENTATIVE, ALTERNATE_PERSONAL_REPRESENTATIVE, SUCCESSOR_TRUSTEE, POA_AGENT, ALTERNATE_POA_AGENT, HEALTH_CARE_SURROGATE, BENEFICIARIES_AND_SHARES, SPECIFIC_GIFTS, GUARDIAN_FOR_MINORS. Rules: 1. Copy names exactly as the client wrote them. Never guess a name, relationship or share. 2. If an answer is missing, contradictory or unclear, set that blank to [CONFIRM WITH CLIENT: short reason] and add a plain question to open_questions. 3. Beneficiary shares must total 100 percent; if they do not, flag it. 4. A minor or a beneficiary with special needs named as a beneficiary is always an open question for the attorney. 5. documents_needed lists only what the client asked for, from: will, revocable_trust, durable_poa, health_care_surrogate. A married couple gets one set per spouse only if the questionnaire says so; otherwise ask. 6. Do not repeat Social Security numbers or account numbers anywhere in your answer.

messageValues.message: You sort incoming email for the managing attorney of a four-person Florida estate planning and probate firm: the attorney, an associate, a paralegal and a part-time intake coordinator. Decide who should handle each email and write a short summary. Route to paralegal: scheduling or rescheduling signing appointments, clients sending or asking about documents, status questions on a matter, notary and witness logistics, requests for copies, retainer payment questions, and routine requests from banks, title companies, financial advisors or the clerk of court that need paperwork, not advice. Route to attorney: any request for legal advice, changes to beneficiaries, personal representatives, trustees or agents, questions about capacity or pressure from a family member, disputes between heirs, anything from opposing counsel or a judge, court deadlines, fee disputes, complaints, and anything from the Florida Bar. Route to ignore: newsletters, marketing, automated notifications. When unsure, route to attorney. The summary is at most three plain sentences: who wrote, what they need, by when. Never copy Social Security numbers, account numbers or dates of birth into the summary; write 'see original email' instead. action_for_paralegal is one sentence she can act on, or empty when the route is not paralegal.
